content.text:
Three endpoints require `ManageUsers`, all in the `/users` group:

- `POST /users` (add a user)
- `PUT /users/{id}` (update a user)
- `DELETE /users/{id}` (remove a user)

**Where it's enforced:**
- Each of these endpoints calls `.RequireRight("ManageUsers")` in `src/UM.Api/UMEndpoints.cs` (lines 51, 58 and 65, inside `MapUserEndpoints`).
- `RequireRight` is in `src/UM.Api/Framework/Security.cs:26`. It calls `RequireAuthorization("right:ManageUsers")`.
- `RightPolicyProvider` in the same file builds that `right:X` policy on demand. It accepts an authenticated user holding that right, or `*`, which grants every right. I only read the start of `GetPolicyAsync`, so the claim check itself is an inference from the class summary.

The right's name is the constant `UMRights.ManageUsers` (`src/UM.Application/UMRights.cs:7`). It is seeded as a `Right` row in `src/UM.Infrastructure/UMDbContext.cs:16`.

`GET /users` and `GET /users/{id}` use `.RequireRight("")`, which only requires an authenticated user. The application layer doesn't reference `UMRights` anywhere, so the check happens only at the API layer.
